text:
sara: Hey team — customer (acme-app) reports GitHub OAuth failing during callback. They see a 403 with our /auth/callback handler. Works when they hit the callback URL directly, but fails when going through their corporate proxy.

sara: Error they pasted: `Callback rejected: invalid_state_or_host` (our app logs `oauth: host validation failed`).

sara: Repro notes from customer: full flow completes on GitHub and redirects to `https://app.acme.com/auth/callback?code=...&state=abc123`, but our app immediately returns 403.

daniel: Do we validate the Host header against the redirect_uri in the session?

sara: Yes, we compare request.Host (and port) to the redirect_uri host stored in the session for extra safety. If mismatch -> reject.

kevin: Could be proxy rewriting Host to internal LB name (e.g., `lb.internal`) and not preserving original host. Customer mentioned an edge proxy that terminates TLS and forwards to our backend.

sara: Customer confirmed the upstream proxy rewrites Host header to `internal-lb` and sets `X-Forwarded-Host: app.acme.com`. They do not forward the original port.

infra-bot: Suggestion: check that `preserve_host` / `proxy_set_header Host $http_host` is enabled on their proxy. Also ensure our app is behind a trusted proxy list so we use X-Forwarded-* headers when set.

support_anna: Customer asked for a quick workaround — can we relax host validation for that tenant temporarily?

daniel: We can add a per-tenant toggle but prefer not to ship a global relaxation. For immediate triage we can add the proxy's `lb.internal` to the allowed hostnames for that tenant and log the change.

kevin: Also double-check cookie/session domain + SameSite. If the proxy changes scheme (https -> http) or port, the session cookie might be considered insecure and not included, which would lead to an invalid state. Customer flow shows state param present but session missing.

sara: Good point — customer logs show `Set-Cookie: session=; Secure; SameSite=Lax` on initial redirect but subsequent callback from proxy arrives without session cookie.

support_anna: Repro steps we asked customer to try: 1) curl the callback endpoint with original Host header: `curl -I -H \"Host: app.acme.com\" \"https://<backend-ip>/auth/callback?code=...&state=abc123\"` 2) curl without Host header to see difference.

sara: Customer ran those: with Host header -> 200; without -> 403. Confirms Host header matters.

daniel: Action items: 1) ask infra to confirm proxy preserves Host and forwards X-Forwarded-Proto and X-Forwarded-Host. 2) Support to request temporary allowed-host entry for tenant `acme-app` (only while they reconfigure) 3) Add diagnostic logs to surface when host validation fails (include raw Host header, X-Forwarded-Host, session id presence).

kevin: If proxy can't be changed, we can support honoring X-Forwarded-Host when it comes from a trusted proxy IP range. Need infra to provide their egress IPs.

sara: Customer will coordinate with their network team. I've given them the diagnostic curl and asked for proxy config (nginx/HAProxy/Cloudflare worker).

support_anna: For the ticket: note we did not see PKCE/state corruption — state param intact — problem is host mismatch -> session cookie not sent -> state appears invalid.

infra-bot: Ticket checklist added: request proxy config, request trace-id/sample logs, advise enabling `preserve_host` and forwarding `X-Forwarded-*` headers, optionally add `allowed_host` entry. :white_check_mark:

kevin: I'll open a short-lived PR to add more verbose host-validate logging so we can resolve quickly if this happens again.

sara: Thanks — keeping ticket owner while customer confirms proxy changes. :eyes:
